claim: When the claim gives a function name and a line, and exactly one function has that exact name, place_claim takes it and ignores the line, even if the line is inside a different function (a method with the same short name). The claim is placed on the wrong function.
what_goes_wrong: An imported finding that gives a short method name plus a line inside that method is placed on a same-named top-level function, so the worker tests the wrong code and the claim is judged against the wrong target.
fix_idea: When a line is given, prefer the candidate (exact or suffix match) whose range contains the line, and use the exact-name-only shortcut only when no line is given or the line is in that function.

claim: For a SARIF file the --source option replaces the tool name that the SARIF run itself gives (driver name), although --source is documented as the name of the tool only for a finding that does not give one.
what_goes_wrong: With a SARIF file, `import --source X` overwrites the tool name the SARIF run gives, so findings from bandit are recorded as X, contradicting the documented fallback-only meaning of --source.
fix_idea: In sarif_entries use `text_of(driver name) or source or "outside"`, matching the JSON path.

claim: For a SARIF file, the `source` argument overrides the tool name that the file gives in tool.driver.name. The docstring and the --source help say `source` is only for an entry that does not give one (the hpflow form does this right).
what_goes_wrong: With `import --findings x.sarif --source NAME`, every SARIF result is labelled NAME instead of the tool name in tool.driver.name, so the finding source is wrong, unlike the hpflow form.
fix_idea: In sarif_entries use the driver name first and fall back to source: text_of(driver name) or source or "outside".
